walkthroughs.body_html:
Weather is what you see out the window today. Climate is the long-term pattern.

A rainy day in July is weather. The fact that UK summers are mild and wet is climate.

The UK has a temperate maritime climate: cool summers, mild winters, rainfall all year.

This is because we sit at mid-latitude (50-60°N), surrounded by sea, with the warm North Atlantic Drift keeping us mild.

The UK is influenced by five main air masses:

Tropical maritime (SW): warm, wet.
Tropical continental (S): hot, dry (summer heatwaves).
Polar maritime (NW): cool, showery.
Polar continental (E): cold, dry (winter freezes).
Arctic maritime (N): very cold, snow.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.
Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
Climate change only happens in summer.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Climate change only happens in summer.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.

mcqs.q: What weather does an anticyclone (high pressure system) bring?
options: Descending air warms and dries, suppressing cloud formation — so anticyclones bring clear, settled weather: hot in summer, cold and frosty in winter.
Climate change only happens in summer.
High pressure brings stormy weather because the air pushes down hard.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
